title.narrative: Output 1.4. Strengthened social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative: Government in consultation with the Social Partners revised the Employment Act (1982) culminating in the drafting of the Employment Amendment Bill that was adopted by the Labour Advisory Board in July 2021 and submitted to Cabinet for approval by end October 2021. (To be confirmed) From May to November 2020, the ILO analysed provisions of the draft Employment Bill and proposed improvements to the Bill in line with International Labour Standards and the comments of the ILO Committee of Experts. Reference to the comments of the Supervisory Bodies included the following; Observation (CEACR) - adopted 2019, focusing on the Equal Remuneration Convention, 1951 (No. 100); Observation (CEACR) adopted 2019, focusing on the Discrimination (Employment and Occupation) Convention, 1958 adopted in 2020; Observation (CEACR) adopted in 2017 focusing on the Minimum Age Convention 1973 (No. 138); Direct Request (CEACR) adopted 2018, published 108th ILC session (2019) focusing on the Protection of Wages Convention, 1949 (No. 95). The ILO inputs and comments on the Employment Bill were consolidated into a Technical Memorandum that was presented to the tripartite Labour Advisory Board in May 2021.

Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity of labour administrations

description.narrative: The Labour Inspectorate of the Ministry of Labour & Social Security developed and adopted a Strategic Compliance Plan in May 2021. The Strategic Compliance Plan is being implemented by the labour inspectorate in the retail and security sectors. The plan assists the labour inspectorate to improve its delivery in promoting compliance in collaboration with other actors in the targeted sectors. The compliance issues targeted by the Plan are notably, non-payment of wages and failure by employers to pay statutory deductions. To this end, compliance measures in the plan seek to promote enforcement interventions for the aforementioned compliance issues; to promote systemic interventions intended to streamline the issuance of compliance certificates for employers who intend to apply for public contracts in the Swaziland Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (SPPRA); collaboration and joint campaigns with the National Provident Fund to enforce remittance of statutory deductions made from workers' salaries; and finally education and awareness raising campaign for both employers and workers in the two sectors on the provisions of legislation on the compliance issues identified. The plan is underpinned by the core elements of labour inspections as defined by Convention No. 81 and No. 129. At the time of this reporting, the strategic compliance plan in Eswatini was well underway with 67% (25/37) of actions devised in the plan completed. This includes 62% of the enforcement intervention, 69% of the communication intervention, and 75% of the systemic interventions completed. ILO facilitated a Strategic Compliance training for 20 labour inspectors from the Eswatini Ministry of Labour & Social Security in April 2021. Some of the key objectives of the training workshop were to introduce the Strategic Compliance Planning methodology to achieve compliance outcomes, to provide guidance on how to develop a Strategic Compliance Plan based on available resources and on how to pilot it in selected priority sectors. Additional objectives of the training were to build capacity of the inspectors on the use of the Strategic Compliance Planning Portal, and to assist the inspectors to develop a short term inspection strategy for a discreet compliance issue. Focusing on the retail and security sectors, a draft Strategic Compliance Plan was developed at the training workshop and later refined for adoption by the Ministry of Labour and Social Security in May 2021. Ongoing ILO advisory support is provided towards the implementation of the Strategic Compliance Plan since it was adopted by the Ministry of Labour & Social Security in May 2021. The ILO made inputs into awareness raising messages communicated in brochures meant to sensitize employers and workers on provisions of the law to enhance compliance in the identified sectors. In particular, the messages address the issue of the protection of workers in the retail sector (hairdressers and retail) in which there is a predominance of women.

description.narrative: The government gazetted and published the Disaster Management COVID-19 Regulations 2020 of which Third Schedule provides for Safe return to work. The Schedule provides for safety and health of persons at workplace and for protection of other persons against hazards to safety and health arising during the COVID19 pandemic, by specifying roles and responsibilities of employers, workers and Occupational Health and Safety inspectors. The Fourth Schedule of the Regulations requires provision of psychosocial support, including sensitization to and monitoring for gender-based violence. In May 2021, ILO collaborated with the African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD) to facilitate a series of online trainings on OSH and COVID-19 to the Eswatini OSH practitioners. The topics covered in these online trainings included the following; Setting up COVID-19 coordination team and work streams, Epidemiology and management of COVID-19 in the workplace, Return to work post COVID-19 illness & lock-down, implications of COVID-19 in the workplace, as well as COVID-19 Health Risk Assessment and workplace control measures. The trainings also entailed the sharing of a series of Guidelines on COVID-19 and OSH. The knowledge gained from the trainings and guidelines shared during the training organized by the ILO and AUDA-NEPAD contributed towards the development of the Eswatini Disaster Management COVID-19 Regulations that were gazetted and published by Government in November 2020. The ILO also collaborated with the secretariat of the SADC Employment and Labour Sector in June 2020, to host and facilitate a webinar on COVID-19 for labour and OSH inspectors and representatives of the Social Partners, in which representatives from Eswatini participated. In September 2021, the ILO collaborated with the African Regional Labour Administration Centre (ARLAC) to host and facilitate a virtual tripartite workshop focusing on promoting workplace compliance with OSH policies, systems, programmes and legal frameworks.
